name: Igloo Inc.
oneLine: Web3 holding company told as a full-screen WebGL arctic scene; cinematic 3D first, text as sparse HUD.

palette.note: Body/loader fill: a cold blue-grey slate shown before the WebGL scene paints
Fogged distant snow ridges; the atmospheric haze layer behind the igloo
Mid-tone snow terrain and ice-block faces in the rendered scene
Deepest ice-block shadows; the only near-dark value, kept blue not black
Glowing seams between ice blocks and the white HUD labels / wordmark
HUD text blocks and constellation line overlays drawn on top of the 3D

type.note: 'IGLOO' at ~32px tall, double-stroke rounded square letterforms, white, top-left corner only
~10-11px uppercase-ish code strings in white bars, four corners of the viewport, reads like telemetry readouts
Mobile loader is a 20px ASCII progress string '----===+++' centered on slate, glowing white

layout: No DOM layout in the usual sense: one fixed 100vh canvas with HUD text pinned to four corners (logo + status top-left, data block top-right, legal/sound bottom-left).
Content density is extremely low: each scroll position is a single staged 3D composition, the igloo dead-center, with ~60px corner margins for the HUD.

Sections are camera shots, not blocks: scroll-1 is a high aerial of the finished igloo, scroll-2 a ground-level view with blocks lifting apart and numbered nodes (32, 33, 47, 22) connected by thin lines.
motion: Scroll scrubs a 3D camera and an exploding-assembly of the igloo: blocks visibly lift and rotate apart between scroll-1 and scroll-2.
Thin white constellation lines with node labels are drawn over the 3D, linking specific ice blocks like a data graph.
(inferred) HUD strings scramble/decode character-by-character as sections change; the corner text in screenshots is mid-glyph-scramble.

(inferred) Loader string '----===+++' advances as assets stream in, then the slate cross-fades into the snow scene; Awwwards Site of the Year 2024 write-ups cite its sound design and scroll-driven WebGL.
interactions: Scroll is the only real control: it drives camera position and assembly state continuously.
(inferred) Cursor parallax on the scene and a sound toggle in the bottom-left HUD block.
steal: Corner-pinned mono HUD (mission time, orbit, channel count, anomaly rate) framing our hero visualization, like Igloo's four-corner data blocks.
Exploded-view-on-scroll for the model architecture section: encoder/decoder blocks separate as the user scrolls, with numbered nodes joined by 1px lines.
Text scramble/decode effect on section labels and metric values in the results section, mimicking telemetry resolving from noise.
leave: A blank slate loader gating all content: recruiters skim in seconds, so our first paint must show the headline and a real chart, not a progress string.
Fully canvas-rendered text: it is unreadable to screen readers and search; our HUD labels should be real DOM text over the canvas.
